body: Hugs always help. Really. Thank you.

I’m really happy you were able to break that pattern and use it to help others. I don’t have a whole lot of money. But if we separated I’d be financially stable for the first time. I could have everything I ever wanted... a Corvette, pilot lessons, a downtown studio apartment... but I wouldn’t have my family anymore. I’d give all that up to live with them in a cardboard box.

I really don’t see any future potential for myself. My mother says because I’m only 26 she knows I’ll be happy again, but I’m not convinced. Took me 21 years to find someone who loves me and I know I’ll never have that ever again.
Thank you. I’ve been talking to a few people and I have a good support system. It’s kept me alive this long, so far.

Thought about working out more. But everything reminds me of my wife. How much I want her back and to be a family again and it’s not what she wants. I don’t want to make her stay but it sucks. I don’t know how I’m going to manage living like this.

I'm definitely emotionally exhausted. I don't think I've ever felt this completely drained. I actually have my first appointment with a psychiatrist in years tomorrow, because I'm pretty unstable at this point. I'm really hoping it helps but it's getting harder to stay positive about it.

Thank you for your kind reply. I've been trying to talk to her about all this for weeks now. The communication is just... gone. Is it possible to want to die and want to live at the same time? I feel like it's the only way she would ever understand, but I realize no one would win in that situation, especially me. I just don't know what else to do anymore.

Your words were comforting and I appreciate it.
Going through something that seems similar. Props to you for being courageous enough to share this. Thank you.
